observations.body: Paul names adultery, murder, theft, false testimony, and coveting, then says the commands are summed up in love of neighbor and that love fulfills the law.
observations.label: Neighbor-love is said to fulfill named commands

observations.body: Neighbor-love is said to fulfill named commands belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Romans 13:8–10 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Romans 13:8–10 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: Neighbor-love is said to fulfill named commands belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
payload.title: Neighbor-love is said to fulfill named commands
